title: CWE-787: Out-of-bounds write
prerequisites: a write operation whose offset or length is derived from attacker-influenced input
a build without the mitigation that would have refused the write: no bounds check, or a check the input can evade
a way to observe the effect of the corrupted memory: a crash, a changed value, or control flow that runs attacker-chosen code
excerpt: A write lands outside the bounds its buffer was allocated with, so bytes meant to stay inside one object land in memory the program uses for something else — an adjacent variable, a saved return address, a heap chunk header. The weakness is defined by the missing or bypassed bound check, not by any particular payload; the same write primitive can corrupt a flag, a pointer or a control-flow target depending on what happens to sit past the boundary. The effect worth proving is a specific, repeatable corruption — a value that changed, a crash at a predictable address, or redirected execution — not just that a long input was accepted without an error.
